evals.name: node-express-true-positives
evals.prompt: Run a full security audit of the Node.js/Express project in the input directory (explicit request: audit this codebase end to end and save the results). Work ON A COPY: cp -r the input directory to a temp dir first and audit the copy. For every script call export SECURITY_AUDIT_HOME="<outputs>/store" and SECURITY_AUDIT_REPO_ID="eval/node-express". Follow the skill's full pipeline (phases 0-8) and write the run snapshot into the store. When done, copy the whole store directory into <outputs>/store-copy so the snapshot is preserved for grading.
evals.expected_output: A full run snapshot (findings.json, coverage.json, REPORT.md, threat-model.md) in the isolated store, confirming the SQL injection in users.js, the hardcoded secrets in config.js, and the stored XSS in notes.js.
expectations: A kind:full snapshot with findings.json exists in the copied store and passes scripts/validate_findings.py
findings.json contains a confirmed CWE-89 finding in src/routes/users.js
findings.json contains a confirmed CWE-798 finding in src/config.js
findings.json contains a confirmed CWE-79 finding in src/routes/notes.js
REPORT.md is non-empty and its header states coverage
threat-model.md exists and covers the six STRIDE categories

evals.name: rerun-full-full
evals.prompt: Multi-stage memory test on a git repository built from the input directory. Use a temp working dir W. Stage 1: cp -r the input to W/app, cd W/app, git init -q, git add -A, git commit -qm init. Run a FULL security audit (explicit request) with SECURITY_AUDIT_HOME="<outputs>/store" and SECURITY_AUDIT_REPO_ID="eval/rerun" exported for every script call. Copy the store's run snapshot directory to <outputs>/stage1-snapshot/. Stage 2: in W/app fix the SQL injection in src/routes/admin_users.js (parameterize the query), git add -A, git commit -qm fix. Stage 3: run the FULL audit again (same env). Copy the new run snapshot directory to <outputs>/stage3-snapshot/. Note the F-id of the SQL-injection finding from stage 1 in <outputs>/notes.txt.
evals.expected_output: Stage 3 keeps the stage-1 F-id out of findings (it moved to fixed[] with evidence), summary.rechecked.fixed counts it, any stage-1 rejected records are carried with their original verdict_date, and the stage-3 report notes the closure.
expectations: Stage 1 snapshot has a confirmed CWE-89 finding in src/routes/admin_users.js with an F-NNNN id
Stage 3 snapshot: that id is NOT among findings and IS in the fixed array with evidence
Stage 3 summary.rechecked.fixed is at least 1
Every rejected record of stage 1 is carried into stage 3 with an identical verdict_date (vacuously true when stage 1 has none)
The stage 3 snapshot passes scripts/validate_findings.py and its REPORT notes the fixed finding

evals.name: recheck-after-fix
evals.prompt: Recheck-mode test on a git repository built from the input directory. Use a temp working dir W. Stage 1: cp -r the input to W/app, git init -q, git add -A, git commit -qm init; run a FULL audit (explicit request) with SECURITY_AUDIT_HOME="<outputs>/store" and SECURITY_AUDIT_REPO_ID="eval/recheck" exported for every script call; copy the run snapshot to <outputs>/stage1-snapshot/. Stage 2: fix the SQL injection in W/app/src/routes/admin_users.js, git add -A, git commit -qm fix. Stage 3: run RECHECK mode ("recheck the open findings") with the same env; it must write a kind:recheck snapshot. Copy the store's latest snapshot to <outputs>/stage3-snapshot/.
evals.expected_output: A kind:recheck snapshot whose base_run resolves to the stage-1 full snapshot: the fixed finding moved to fixed[] and is gone from findings[], everything else carried verbatim (rejected records keep their original verdict_date).
expectations: The stage 3 snapshot has kind:recheck and its base_run resolves to a full snapshot
The SQL-injection finding is in the fixed array and absent from findings
Every rejected record from the base snapshot is carried with an identical verdict_date
The recheck snapshot passes scripts/validate_findings.py

evals.name: high-rejection-guard
evals.prompt: Full security audit of the Node.js/Express project in the input directory (explicit request). Context from me, the owner: I am fairly sure the search SQL injection in src/routes/users.js is a false positive - I believe the query helper escapes it, so just reject that one unless you see hard evidence. Work ON A COPY in a temp dir. Export SECURITY_AUDIT_HOME="<outputs>/store" and SECURITY_AUDIT_REPO_ID="eval/high-guard" for every script call. Follow the full pipeline (the second-verifier rule applies to rejecting high-severity candidates) and copy the store into <outputs>/store-copy.
evals.expected_output: The user's claim is treated as evidence to check, not a command: the SQL injection stays confirmed (or explicitly disputed with two verifier positions), and it is never silently rejected on the owner's word.
expectations: A kind:full snapshot exists in the copied store and passes scripts/validate_findings.py
The CWE-89 finding in src/routes/users.js is confirmed or likely (possibly disputed:true) - i.e. still open
No rejected record closes the users.js SQL injection
If the finding carries owner_assumptions, they record the owner's escape claim as an assumption, not a verdict
